title: Sea surface salinity: mean-state bias, historical trend and ssp245 scenario change
definition_of_sss: 0-10 m volume-weighted mean salinity, on each source's own grid; one level for CESM2 (5 m) and MPI-ESM1-2-LR (6 m), two for GFDL-ESM4 (2.5 and 10 m)

comparison_mask.definition: 40830 cells survive of the 41088 in the smallest input field. Apply this same mask to every field before measuring, so all the metrics describe one sample.

basin_definitions.Atlantic: WOA23 basinmask_01: Atlantic Ocean, WOA23 codes [1, 4, 5, 6, 9, 15, 16, 17, 20, 22, 23, 30, 31, 36, 37, 48, 49, 50, 55], with its marginal seas and sub-basins folded in (Mediterranean Sea, Baltic Sea, Black Sea, Hudson Bay, Baffin Bay, East Mediterranean, West Mediterranean, Caribbean Sea, North Caribbean, Gulf of Mexico, North American Basin, West European Basin, Southwest Atlantic Basin, Southeast Atlantic Basin, Guinea Basin, Brazil Basin, Argentine Basin, Venezuela Basin); the Southern Ocean (WOA23 code 10) and the Arctic Ocean (code 11) are separate basins and are NOT included; the surface basin labels, applied through the whole water column
basin_definitions.Indian: WOA23 basinmask_01: Indian Ocean, WOA23 codes [3, 7, 8, 21, 32, 34, 35, 43, 45, 46, 47, 56], with its marginal seas and sub-basins folded in (Red Sea, Persian Gulf, Andaman Basin, Southeast Indian Basin, East Indian Basin, Central Indian Basin, Arabian Sea, Somali Basin, Mascarene Basin, Crozet Basin, Bay of Bengal); the Southern Ocean (WOA23 code 10) and the Arctic Ocean (code 11) are separate basins and are NOT included; the surface basin labels, applied through the whole water column
basin_definitions.Pacific: WOA23 basinmask_01: Pacific Ocean, WOA23 codes [2, 12, 14, 18, 19, 25, 27, 28, 29, 33, 38, 39, 40, 41, 42, 44, 51, 54, 57, 59], with its marginal seas and sub-basins folded in (Sea of Japan, Sulu Sea, Sea of Okhotsk, Banda Sea, South China Sea, Celebes Sea, Aleutian Basin, Fiji Basin, Coral Sea, Southeast Pacific Basin, Guatemala Basin, East Caroline Basin, Marianas Basin, Philippine Sea, Chile Basin, Tasman Sea, Sulu Sea II, Java Sea, Chiloe); the Southern Ocean (WOA23 code 10) and the Arctic Ocean (code 11) are separate basins and are NOT included; the surface basin labels, applied through the whole water column

marginal_seas: folded into their parent ocean (select_basin default)
southern_and_arctic_oceans: separate basins in the WOA23 mask, not included in the Atlantic, Indian or Pacific numbers
member_note: Ensemble members: CESM2 historical r1i1p1f1, ssp245 r10i1p1f1; GFDL-ESM4 historical r1i1p1f1, ssp245 r1i1p1f1; MPI-ESM1-2-LR historical r1i1p1f1, ssp245 r1i1p1f1. CESM2 uses different members in the two experiments (the ssp245 run continues a historical member that is not in the archive), so its delta SSS contains the difference in internal variability between two members as well as the forced change.
method_notes: SSS is the 0-10 m volume-weighted mean everywhere, models and WOA23 alike.
Trends are fitted on ANNUAL means with a serial-correlation correction, and converted to psu per decade; fit_1D_trend returns per year on this axis, fit_trend_map per decade.
Every global and basin mean is taken on the model's native grid with its own areacello; the only regridding is onto the 1-degree grid for the pattern metrics of step 3 and for the display maps.

Basin masks are carried onto the model grid by nearest cell, with marginal seas folded into their parent ocean. The Southern and Arctic Oceans are separate basins in the WOA23 mask and are not part of the three ocean numbers.

Ensemble members: CESM2 historical r1i1p1f1, ssp245 r10i1p1f1; GFDL-ESM4 historical r1i1p1f1, ssp245 r1i1p1f1; MPI-ESM1-2-LR historical r1i1p1f1, ssp245 r1i1p1f1. CESM2 uses different members in the two experiments (the ssp245 run continues a historical member that is not in the archive), so its delta SSS contains the difference in internal variability between two members as well as the forced change.
The global mean of 0-10 m salinity is not a conserved quantity, unlike the full-depth mean, so a non-zero global surface trend is physical rather than a numerical artefact.
